principles: Games must remain playable without a 420 Wallet unless a game explicitly documents a separate non-420 requirement.
Wallet connection expands ownership, interoperability, prestige, ecosystem participation or optional content rather than serving as a mandatory core-game admission gate.
Guest profiles, ordinary saves, anti-cheat and routine gameplay state remain off-chain by default.
Only provenance-sensitive identity links, entitlements, migration commitments and cross-game attestations belong in the canonical protocol layer.
420 Wallet and Capability Registry remain authoritative for wallet ownership, sessions and execution; Gaming Protocol creates no parallel wallet authority.
Cross-game consumers query explicit known attestations or entitlements; the protocol exposes no canonical global player-activity enumeration surface.
invariants: GAME-INV-001: registering, updating or disabling a game is default-deny and capability-authorized.
GAME-INV-002: an active registered game may be joined by a wallet account without administrator approval.
GAME-INV-003: one wallet account has at most one canonical profile per game namespace in v1.
GAME-INV-004: only the registered game operator may issue or revoke that game's entitlements, migration claims and cross-game attestations.
GAME-INV-005: migration claims are target-account-bound, expiry-aware and single-consumption.
GAME-INV-006: entitlement and attestation revocation is fail-closed.
GAME-INV-007: inactive games cannot create new canonical player profiles.
GAME-INV-008: no contract in this suite stores seed phrases, private keys, session signing material, cloud-save data or raw guest progression.
GAME-INV-009: game-specific mechanics remain outside the shared genesis protocol.
GAME-INV-010: connecting a wallet does not itself grant pay-to-win statistical advantages.
